svg.desc: Top view of the 141.35 by 141.35 inch BIOBUZZ field, audience at the bottom, red alliance on the left. Route self_garden_topup_park for the RED alliance, starting in tile B1, with 10 steps: 1 START at (44.5, 12.2, -110 deg); 2 SHOOT 4 at UP cell from (44.5, 12.2, -110 deg); 3 DRIVE into the GARDEN constant to 9.5, 10.6; 4 INTAKE GARDEN +4 from (9.5, 10.6, -90 deg); 5 DRIVE back to the shot linear to 44.5, 12.2; 6 SHOOT 4 at AUDIENCE cell from (44.5, 12.2, -110 deg); 7 DRIVE along the wall constant to 30.0, 14.8; 8 DRIVE corridor reverse tangent to 30.0, 84.0; 9 DRIVE to the zone linear to 12.0, 92.2; 10 PARK at (12.0, 92.2, 0 deg). First tip: we shoot the first tip. Estimated 21.8 s, POLLEN balance -4, up to 28 points for our robot; 0 errors and 2 warnings.

g.title: Where a robot facing -110 degrees may be set up (rule G304): the tinted stretches of the own walls. The gaps are the FLOWERS, the LOADING ZONE, the corners and the center line.
g.text: tinted: where this start may stand (G304)

g.title: step 3: DRIVE into the GARDEN constant to 9.5, 10.6 (t = 5.5 to 7.1 s) - Slides along the audience wall to the GARDEN with the intake toward it and stops with the front edge 0.8 in off the wall, in front of the row of POLLEN.
step 5: DRIVE back to the shot linear to 44.5, 12.2 (t = 10.1 to 11.6 s) - Back to the pose of the first volley, turning evenly while it slides away from the wall.

step 7: DRIVE along the wall constant to 30.0, 14.8 (t = 17.1 to 18.3 s) - Slides sideways along the audience wall with the front still toward it, 5 in off the wall, until it is beside the left corridor.

step 8: DRIVE corridor reverse tangent to 30.0, 84.0 (t = 18.3 to 20.5 s) - Backwards (the shooter end first) up the left corridor, 13 in clear of the HIVE keep-out and of the spill zone of the cell that tipped.
step 9: DRIVE to the zone linear to 12.0, 92.2 (t = 20.5 to 21.8 s) - Turns to face +x while it slides into the LOADING ZONE.

step 1: START at (44.5, 12.2, -110 deg) (t = 0.0 to 0.0 s) - A front corner ON the audience wall, turned 20 degrees clockwise, back toward the audience cell. Chosen because the robot comes back to it for the second volley: it is a shooting pose AND 13 in closer to the GARDEN than the anchor start, which saves about 1.0 s on the two trips to it, against the anchor start. The same pose is used twice, so the aim only has to be checked once. (On a route with only one trip the same start saves just 0.4 s, which is not worth the harder placement.)

step 2: SHOOT 4 at UP cell from (44.5, 12.2, -110 deg) (t = 0.0 to 5.5 s) - The first tip. The UP cell holds 3 NECTAR, so the 3rd POLLEN tips the HIVE (+20) and the 4th is the spare for a field that needs one more. The camera stops the feeder only about 0.85 s after the tip, so the 4th is probably launched too and spent: that is the WARN on this step, and it is fine, it is only the spare. The robot fires from where it was put, with no drive first. Real teams land only about 6 shots in 10, so plan on this volley tipping the HIVE less than half of the time (the top-up routes are for that).

step 4: INTAKE GARDEN +4 from (9.5, 10.6, -90 deg) (t = 7.1 to 10.1 s) - The 4 GARDEN POLLEN lie in a row along the wall. After the first volley the robot holds 0 (the spare was probably spent), so it can take all 4 (G407: never more than 4). If the feeder did stop in time the robot holds 1 and the intake must stop at 3: the runner stops at 4.

step 6: SHOOT 4 at AUDIENCE cell from (44.5, 12.2, -110 deg) (t = 11.6 to 17.1 s) - THE TOP-UP. The plan says the first volley tipped the HIVE, so on paper the audience cell is already DOWN: that is the WARN on this step. On the field the robot fires only if its camera still shows the audience cell UP (tags in view, steady), which means the first volley did not tip it; the cell then still holds the 3 NECTAR and whatever landed, so 1 to 3 more POLLEN tip it. If the camera shows the cell DOWN (the HIVE tipped), or sees nothing, the volley is skipped and the robot goes on. The plan counts the volley's time (5.5 s) as if it fired, so the finish time is the worst case.

step 10: PARK at (12.0, 92.2, 0 deg) (t = 21.8 to 21.8 s) - Parks in the LOWER half of the LOADING ZONE, overlapping it by 6.5 in (PARK needs 3), the whole robot 4 in off the red wall so the LEAVE is kept too (touching ANY wall at the end of AUTO loses it, QA21). The upper half of the zone stays free for the partner.

POLLEN: hold 4 at start, +4 taken, -8 fired, 0 at the end (balance -4) | Validator: 0 ERROR, 2 WARN

g.title: WARN step 2 [G417] step 2 (SHOOT): the HIVE tips with POLLEN 3 of the 4 (3 NECTAR in the cell; a cell tips at 8 POLLEN-equivalents (each POLLEN counts 1, each NECTAR 5/3)), but the camera cannot stop the feeder at once: the POLLEN that tips it is in the air for 0.50 s and the feeder stops about 0.85 s after it lands (Auto.TIP_STOP_LATENCY_SEC), while the next POLLEN leaves 1.00 s after the last. So the next 1 POLLEN will probably be launched into the cell while it swings down (G417: a launch at a rocking HIVE can spoil the tip; QA12 lets you add elements to a HIVE that is moving) and is spent: the plan counts 4 fired and 0 of the spare kept. The spare is for a field that needs one more POLLEN, not a POLLEN to carry on. Fire only 3 to keep it for sure (no spare then), or measure the real stop time on day one: with a latency under 0.50 s the spare stays in the robot
